lessons.title: Service managers
lessons.summary: What is a service manager responsible for? Managing configured service lifecycle and supervision.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A running process and a healthy service are different observations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service is active but its endpoint returns errors. Inspect application health and logs alongside unit status.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Starting a service proves all business operations succeed. This is not a sound assumption; managing configured service lifecycle and supervision.

lessons.takeaway: A running process and a healthy service are different observations.

lessons.title: Enable versus start
lessons.summary: What does enabling a systemd service generally configure? Activation through configured unit installation relationships such as boot targets.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Enabling and starting are separate operations unless explicitly combined.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service works now but does not return after reboot. Inspect enablement and the intended boot activation path.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Enable always starts the process immediately. This is not a sound assumption; activation through configured unit installation relationships such as boot targets.

lessons.takeaway: Enabling and starting are separate operations unless explicitly combined.

lessons.title: Unit overrides
lessons.summary: Why use a systemd drop-in override? Customize a unit without directly editing a vendor-supplied unit file.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Configuration changes may require daemon reload and service action.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A package upgrade replaces local service tuning. Use a managed drop-in and verify the effective unit configuration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Drop-ins are ignored whenever packages update. This is not a sound assumption; customize a unit without directly editing a vendor-supplied unit file.

lessons.takeaway: Configuration changes may require daemon reload and service action.

lessons.title: Journals
lessons.summary: What is journalctl useful for? Querying journal records with filters such as unit and time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Retention and persistence settings determine available history.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A restart failure needs investigation around a known time. Query the relevant unit and time window.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The journal always retains all logs forever. This is not a sound assumption; querying journal records with filters such as unit and time.

lessons.takeaway: Retention and persistence settings determine available history.

lessons.title: Accounts
lessons.summary: Why use separate service accounts? Limit access and attribute activity to distinct workloads.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Account separation must be paired with appropriate permissions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One service account can read unrelated applications' secrets. Separate identities and narrow file and service access.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Separate usernames automatically isolate all files and networks. This is not a sound assumption; limit access and attribute activity to distinct workloads.

lessons.takeaway: Account separation must be paired with appropriate permissions.

lessons.title: SSH keys
lessons.summary: Why protect private SSH keys? Possession can enable authentication wherever the key is trusted.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Key removal and rotation require reviewing authorized locations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A private deployment key appears in a shared log. Revoke or rotate the key and review affected access.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A private key is safe to publish if the username is hidden. This is not a sound assumption; possession can enable authentication wherever the key is trusted.

lessons.takeaway: Key removal and rotation require reviewing authorized locations.

lessons.title: Package management
lessons.summary: Why prefer the distribution package manager for system packages? It tracks package ownership dependencies and updates.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Third-party sources still require trust and version review.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A critical library was installed manually outside package tracking. Inventory the installation and establish a supported update path.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A package manager proves every package is vulnerability-free. This is not a sound assumption; it tracks package ownership dependencies and updates.

lessons.takeaway: Third-party sources still require trust and version review.

lessons.title: Scheduled jobs
lessons.summary: Why define explicit environments for scheduled jobs? They may run with different PATH working directory and credentials.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use explicit paths and controlled output handling.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A script works interactively but fails under the scheduler. Compare identity environment paths and working directory.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Cron always inherits an interactive shell's full environment. This is not a sound assumption; they may run with different PATH working directory and credentials.

lessons.takeaway: Use explicit paths and controlled output handling.

lessons.title: Time synchronization
lessons.summary: Why does consistent system time matter operationally? Authentication log correlation and distributed behavior can depend on it.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Elapsed-time measurement may need monotonic clocks separately.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Authentication failures coincide with clock drift. Inspect synchronization state and correct the time source safely.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Clock synchronization makes all machines perfectly simultaneous forever. This is not a sound assumption; authentication log correlation and distributed behavior can depend on it.

lessons.takeaway: Elapsed-time measurement may need monotonic clocks separately.

lessons.title: Disk layout
lessons.summary: Why separate growth-prone data from critical system paths? Reduce the chance one workload exhausts space needed for core operation.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Capacity limits and monitoring still matter after separation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Application logs fill the root filesystem and disrupt system services. Bound log growth and evaluate storage isolation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Separate directories alone always mean separate capacity. This is not a sound assumption; reduce the chance one workload exhausts space needed for core operation.

lessons.takeaway: Capacity limits and monitoring still matter after separation.

lessons.title: Log rotation
lessons.summary: What should log rotation include beyond renaming files? A retention policy and appropriate application file-handle behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A process may keep writing to a renamed or deleted open file.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Disk usage remains high after a log file was deleted. Inspect open handles and use the application's supported reopen mechanism.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Renaming a log guarantees the process reopens a new file. This is not a sound assumption; a retention policy and appropriate application file-handle behavior.

lessons.takeaway: A process may keep writing to a renamed or deleted open file.

lessons.title: Backups
lessons.summary: What distinguishes a backup from a second live copy? Recoverable retained data protected from relevant failure modes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Replication can propagate accidental deletion or corruption.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An operator deletes data and replication mirrors the deletion. Restore from a verified retained recovery point.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Replication always replaces historical backups. This is not a sound assumption; recoverable retained data protected from relevant failure modes.

lessons.takeaway: Replication can propagate accidental deletion or corruption.

lessons.title: Restore verification
lessons.summary: What should a restore test verify? Data integrity and usable application behavior after recovery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery time and required credentials belong in the test.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A restored database starts but required records are missing. Validate business-relevant data and recovery-point expectations.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A completed file copy proves the application can recover. This is not a sound assumption; data integrity and usable application behavior after recovery.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery time and required credentials belong in the test.

lessons.title: RAID
lessons.summary: What is a limitation of RAID? It does not protect against every logical deletion or corruption event.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Redundancy and independent backups solve different problems.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An administrator deletes a directory on a redundant array. Recover from appropriate backups rather than expecting redundancy to undo deletion.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: RAID makes backups unnecessary. This is not a sound assumption; it does not protect against every logical deletion or corruption event.

lessons.takeaway: Redundancy and independent backups solve different problems.

lessons.title: LVM
lessons.summary: What does logical volume management provide? An abstraction for allocating logical storage from physical capacity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Filesystem resizing requirements are separate from volume resizing.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A logical volume was extended but df shows unchanged capacity. Check and perform the filesystem-specific growth step safely.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Growing a logical volume always grows every filesystem automatically. This is not a sound assumption; an abstraction for allocating logical storage from physical capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Filesystem resizing requirements are separate from volume resizing.

lessons.title: Filesystem mounts
lessons.summary: Why use stable device identifiers in mount configuration? Device enumeration names can change across boots.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Mount configuration should be tested before a critical reboot.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host mounts the wrong volume after device ordering changes. Use stable identifiers and verify mount dependencies.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A disk always keeps the same enumeration name forever. This is not a sound assumption; device enumeration names can change across boots.

lessons.takeaway: Mount configuration should be tested before a critical reboot.

lessons.title: Boot recovery
lessons.summary: What is a safe first step when a host fails after a boot configuration change? Use an authorized recovery path and inspect the specific boot failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Keep a known recovery route before making risky boot changes.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A modified mount entry prevents normal boot. Use recovery access to inspect and correct the faulty entry.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Repeated blind rebooting repairs every configuration error. This is not a sound assumption; use an authorized recovery path and inspect the specific boot failure.

lessons.takeaway: Keep a known recovery route before making risky boot changes.

lessons.title: Patching
lessons.summary: What should a patch rollout include? Representative validation staged deployment and recovery planning.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Some updates require service restart or reboot to take effect.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A kernel update is installed but the old kernel remains running. Plan and verify the required reboot within availability constraints.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Installing a package proves all running processes use the new code. This is not a sound assumption; representative validation staged deployment and recovery planning.

lessons.takeaway: Some updates require service restart or reboot to take effect.

lessons.title: Configuration drift
lessons.summary: Why monitor configuration drift? Untracked changes can undermine reproducibility and policy.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Intentional emergency changes need reconciliation into the managed baseline.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host differs from its declared baseline after incident mitigation. Review the change and adopt or revert it deliberately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every manual change is malicious. This is not a sound assumption; untracked changes can undermine reproducibility and policy.

lessons.takeaway: Intentional emergency changes need reconciliation into the managed baseline.

lessons.title: Access reviews
lessons.summary: Why periodically review privileged access? Roles and operational needs change over time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Removal should account for service dependencies and emergency access.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A departed team member retains production administrative access. Revoke access through the managed identity path and audit related credentials.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Once granted privileged access should never expire. This is not a sound assumption; roles and operational needs change over time.

lessons.takeaway: Removal should account for service dependencies and emergency access.

lessons.title: Sudo policy
lessons.summary: Why scope sudo permissions carefully? Privileged commands can expose more capability than their names suggest.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Editors shells and writable command paths can enable escalation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A restricted sudo rule permits a tool that can launch arbitrary shells. Review effective capabilities and narrow the allowed operation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Allowing any editor as root is always harmless. This is not a sound assumption; privileged commands can expose more capability than their names suggest.

lessons.takeaway: Editors shells and writable command paths can enable escalation.

lessons.title: Resource limits
lessons.summary: Why set service-specific resource limits? Contain resource consumption and protect shared capacity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Limits must be tested against legitimate workload needs.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service fails under load after an aggressive descriptor limit. Compare legitimate demand with observed usage and tune deliberately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any low limit improves reliability without trade-offs. This is not a sound assumption; contain resource consumption and protect shared capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Limits must be tested against legitimate workload needs.

lessons.title: System monitoring
lessons.summary: Why monitor both resource and service indicators? Resource pressure and user-visible behavior provide complementary evidence.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A healthy host metric alone does not prove application success.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Users see errors while host resources look normal. Inspect application and dependency indicators alongside host health.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Low CPU guarantees healthy service behavior. This is not a sound assumption; resource pressure and user-visible behavior provide complementary evidence.

lessons.takeaway: A healthy host metric alone does not prove application success.

lessons.title: Immutable hosts
lessons.summary: What is an advantage of replacing hosts from a known image? Reduce divergence caused by accumulated manual changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Persistent data and identity must survive through explicit design.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A manually repaired host cannot be reproduced elsewhere. Capture the intended configuration and rebuild a tested image.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Replacing a host automatically preserves all local mutable data. This is not a sound assumption; reduce divergence caused by accumulated manual changes.

lessons.takeaway: Persistent data and identity must survive through explicit design.

lessons.title: Capacity forecasts
lessons.summary: Why consider growth and failure scenarios in capacity forecasts? Normal averages can underestimate future or degraded-mode demand.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Forecasts should be checked against observed trends and load tests.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Storage growth will exhaust capacity before the procurement lead time. Project the trend and act before the required lead time is consumed.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Current free space guarantees next month's capacity. This is not a sound assumption; normal averages can underestimate future or degraded-mode demand.

lessons.takeaway: Forecasts should be checked against observed trends and load tests.

lessons.title: Remote administration
lessons.summary: Why preserve an independent recovery path during network changes? A faulty change can cut off the primary management connection.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Test and stage changes with a rollback path.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A firewall change risks removing management access. Use staged rules and verified console or rollback access.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An SSH session guarantees permanent recovery access. This is not a sound assumption; a faulty change can cut off the primary management connection.

lessons.takeaway: Test and stage changes with a rollback path.

lessons.title: Data sanitization
lessons.summary: Why distinguish file deletion from secure media disposal? Deleted data may remain recoverable depending on storage and controls.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Disposal procedures must match media technology and sensitivity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A retired disk contains sensitive production data. Follow an approved media-specific sanitization or destruction process.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Deleting a filename always overwrites every physical copy. This is not a sound assumption; deleted data may remain recoverable depending on storage and controls.

lessons.takeaway: Disposal procedures must match media technology and sensitivity.

lessons.title: Fleet changes
lessons.summary: Why use staged rollouts for system configuration? Limit impact and observe behavior before wider deployment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Canaries should represent important workload variations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A kernel setting works on one host but harms busy database hosts. Test representative groups and expand with monitored stop criteria.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A successful change on one idle host proves fleet-wide safety. This is not a sound assumption; limit impact and observe behavior before wider deployment.

lessons.takeaway: Canaries should represent important workload variations.

lessons.title: Disaster documentation
lessons.summary: What must recovery documentation include to be usable? Dependencies access requirements verification and responsible owners.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery instructions should be accessible during the failure they address.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A recovery team cannot access the instructions because identity services are down. Provide an authorized resilient documentation and access path.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Documentation stored only on the failed system is sufficient. This is not a sound assumption; dependencies access requirements verification and responsible owners.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery instructions should be accessible during the failure they address.

lessons.title: Change verification
lessons.summary: What should follow a successful administration command? Verify the intended system outcome and relevant side effects.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Exit status is evidence about the command rather than complete service health.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A reload command succeeds but requests still fail. Check service behavior logs and the actual loaded configuration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Exit code zero proves every user workflow is healthy. This is not a sound assumption; verify the intended system outcome and relevant side effects.

lessons.takeaway: Exit status is evidence about the command rather than complete service health.
